newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue-chips close 3.4 pct down on short selling.
newsitem.headline: KL blue-chips close 3.4 pct down on short selling.

text.p: Malaysian blue chips closed 3.42 percent lower, battered down by short selling following capital controls imposed by the central bank, and an unexpectedly large trade deficit for June, dealers and analysts said.
The benchmark Composite Index plumetted 33.48 points to close at 945.08, after hitting a new 1997 low of 944.51.

"There are short players looking to roll over their ringgit positions, but now they are being forced to sell shares. They are scrambling to raise ringgit," said a senior officer at a fund management company in Kuala Lumpur.
"The fall is more to do with Bank Negara's (capital control) measures than the trade data. People are saying that they don't have a game plan and are making ad hoc moves," he added.
Among the most active stocks were large-capitalised issues such as Telekom, Maybank and Tenaga, which fell between 30 cents and 1.10 ringgit.

"The rumour is that a Soros fund has sold 1,000 lots (of 200 shares) of Maybank through Singapore. I have confirmed this with two independent parties," said a dealing manager at a local brokerage house.
On Sunday, central Bank Negara announced restrictions on offer-side ringgit swap transactions, effectively curbing speculative selling of the currency.
Malaysia reported a trade deficit of 2.8 billion ringgit for June late on Monday after a surplus of 156.2 million in May. It exceeded most analysts' estimates.
Analysts said the capital controls and the unexpectedly large trade deficit contributed to the sharp sell-down of Malaysian stocks.
Technology Resources bucked the downtrend, rising eight cents to 3.68 ringgit. On Monday, the company announced a 27 percent increase in net earnings for the six months to June 30, 1997.
"The price held because investors were glad to see the strong earnings growth," said Greg Feldberg, a telecommunications analyst at ABN Amro Hoare Govett.
Small-capitalised issues were also hit badly, falling 1.48 percent, or 7.87 points, to 524.30.
Volume ballooned to 282 million shares valued at 1.67 billion ringgit. Losers swamped gainers 598 to 84.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot August contract fell 29.5 points to 964.0, with 1,862 lots traded. September futures shed 26.4 points to 965.0 with eight lots changing hands.
